rationale: Ceilings for scripts/check-docs-web-vitals.mjs (#474 WBS-H075). Derived from measurement, not from a target: three full passes over the five pages below, Lighthouse 13.4.1 mobile emulation, against the built apps/docs/dist served with gzip, on an Apple silicon laptop.

largestContentfulPaintMs 1340: the worst of the 15 measurements was 1225 ms (components/table). 1340 is that value plus 115 ms, i.e. 9.4% headroom (1225 x 1.094), rounded to a flat number. The other pages measured 904-1222 ms.

totalBlockingTimeMs 150: measured 0 ms on every page in every pass. A 0 ms ceiling would not be a regression guard but a machine test, because Lighthouse derives TBT from real task durations on the host CPU and a slower machine produces long tasks where this one produced none. 150 ms is the top of Lighthouse's green band for mobile TBT, so anything under it still scores well; anything over it means new blocking script, which is the regression worth catching on a static documentation site.

cumulativeLayoutShift 0.05: measured 0.000 on every page in every pass. Half of Lighthouse's 0.1 'good' threshold, rather than 0.000, because a late font swap can shift layout on a slow load without anything having regressed.

minPerformanceScore 0.95: measured 1.00 on every page in every pass. It is mostly, but not only, a backstop over the three ceilings above. Lighthouse 13.4.1 weights the performance score TBT 30%, LCP 25%, CLS 25%, First Contentful Paint 10%, Speed Index 10% (read off auditRefs in a real report, not assumed), so about a fifth of it comes from two metrics no ceiling covers. The runner records firstContentfulPaintMs in its report but does not check it, and there is deliberately no FCP or Speed Index ceiling here: a limit invented rather than measured is not a regression guard, and neither has been measured across passes yet. Until one is, a regression confined to FCP or Speed Index can only be caught by this score, and only once it drags the weighted total under 0.95.

The four limits are not equally strong, and should not be read as such. LCP is the only one set close to a measurement (9.4% above 1225 ms), so it is the only one a gradual slowdown trips. TBT and CLS sit above a measured zero, so their headroom relative to the measurement is unbounded: they catch a change that introduces blocking script or layout shift, not a slide. minPerformanceScore is the only limit that sees FCP and Speed Index at all, but at 0.95 against a measured 1.00 it takes a large regression to trip.
